nodes.text: A track is an expected sequence of steps clipped onto one agent. The pane is where tracks are defined, watched, and edited — the list is definitions, the state on each row is the live attachments underneath them.

Definitions, not runs. Each row carries the shape of the spine on the right and the live state of everything attached to it on the left — status is always dots plus label from the shared palette, never a pill, never honey. Honey is spent once, on Define track.

A definition has no state of its own. The dots are its attachments: one dot + label per state present, straight from the shared palette. No attachments reads plainly as “no attachments”, not as a sixth colour.
Items are the spine you authored; nodes count the branch lanes and review arms underneath. It is the one number that tells you how big an edit you are about to open.
Queue depth is not a property of the track — it counts bees that have this track waiting FIFO behind whatever they are attached to right now.
A hollow brick ring, never a filled dot — deviation is visible, not punished, and it is deliberately not part of the status palette because it is not a state to be in.
One honey moment per pane: the filled Define track. Every selection, tab and count here is neutral gray.

Selecting a track opens the thing itself: the typed spine on the left, and everything hanging off it on the right — who is attached and how far along, who is queued behind, and the one pending edit a sidecar agent has proposed. Honey moves to accept, because that is now the single decision this pane is asking for.
the standing shape for a change that ends in a human verdict and a preview
every changed file, plus the packet it hangs off
both lanes must land before the gate
a human verdict on the packet
ran the suite first, then came back — lint was still installing
Steps are the agent's own to mark. Deviating is allowed — it lands as an exception on the attachment, never a failure on the definition.
skipped Typecheck & lint — ran the suite first
The suite passes but nothing publishes a preview for the human — add the deploy the review desk expects.
nectar · label review — after the gate, before the ask
v3 → v4 · one pending at a time
defined 4d ago · 3 versions · promoted on edit

Nothing defined yet. The pane says what a track is in one sentence, spends its one honey moment on the only thing worth doing here, and offers the second, quieter path — the same proposal loop from board 2, run before the first track exists. One small pixel-art moment, per the personality budget; never wallpaper.

A track is an expected sequence of steps you clip onto one agent. Attaching it injects a standing prompt, so the agent keeps the steps updated as it works — and any deviation lands as a visible exception rather than a failure.
or ask a sidecar agent to draft one — it arrives as a proposal you accept, refine, or discard
WHY THIS EMPTY STATE IS NOT A GALLERY

A starter-template grid is the obvious empty state and the wrong one: a template layer is an explicit non-goal. So the affordance is the real verb — define one — and the fallback is an agent drafting a real definition you then judge.

A machine is a canvas with triggers built in, holding many jobs, alive for years. A track is the small thing: one agent, one expected sequence. Tracks work on agents inside machines, but neither feature needs the other.
The track is a real object in Honeybee. This pane is a view onto hive track define / attach / status — the footer says so quietly rather than pretending the pane owns the data.
Art tokens are declared separately from chrome tokens on purpose: the bee may be vivid, the UI palette stays restrained, and the two never bleed into each other.
Three panes, three honey moments, one each: Define track · accept · Define a track. Never two at once.
